welcomeWizard.title: Welcome to the OPC UA NodeSet Editor
welcomeWizard.summary: The editor allows users to create an information model (a.k.a. a NodeSet) for a manufacturing asset or process, with the goal of arriving at common, reusable interfaces for accessing data. As a key design principle, all NodeSets should derive from (extend or reuse) other NodeSets. You can start with core and standardized building blocks provided by the OPC Foundation, or import a starting point created by another designer, standards group, or organization.

aboutModelLibraryWizard.title: Managing Workspaces
aboutModelLibraryWizard.intro: Workspaces are collections of Models that can be viewed and modified.
aboutModelLibraryWizard.line1: A Workspace corresponds to an OPC UA Server's AddressSpace.
aboutModelLibraryWizard.line2: A Workspace should include all Models needed to resolve any references.
aboutModelLibraryWizard.line3: A Shared Models can be used by multiple Workspaces and are always read-only.
aboutModelLibraryWizard.line4: A Private Models are local to a specific Workspace and can be edited.

aboutTypeLibraryWizard.title: Managing Models
aboutTypeLibraryWizard.intro: A Model is a collection of Nodes created by a single authority and is identified by a globally unique URI assigned by that authority. Models can be exported in various file formats, with any file containing a Model referred to as a NodeSet. Models can be imported into a Workspace via the UACloudLibrary or by uploading a NodeSet. Additionally, new Types and Instances can be created within private Models and Models can be shared so they can be used by other Workspaces.

aboutModelValidationWizard.title: Validating Models
aboutModelValidationWizard.intro: Authors of OPC UA Companion Specifications can use the tool to check that the document matches the NodeSet. Each private model has a 'validate' button which brings up a page used to upload Word documents and start a test to compare it to the Model. The Word documents must follow the CS guidelines published by the OPC Foundation.
